title: The Particle Model of Matter
seo_title: Grade 7 Science: The Particle Model of Matter Worksheets (MATATAG)
standard_text: Matter is made of tiny particles in constant motion with spaces between them; the particle model explains the properties of solids, liquids and gases and changes of state. (summary of the MATATAG Science curriculum, Grade 7, Quarter 1: Science of Materials)
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 Science worksheets (MATATAG, Quarter 1: Science of Materials): states of matter, the particle model, particles in motion, the kinetic molecular theory and changes of state. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: All matter is made of tiny particles that are always moving.
body_html:
How to think about it

An atom has a nucleus with protons (positive) and neutrons (no charge), surrounded by electrons (negative). Atoms join to form molecules (H2O, O2).

The particle model: particles in a solid are packed tightly and vibrate in place; in a liquid they are close but move past each other; in a gas they are far apart and move fast. Heating makes particles move faster, causing expansion, melting and boiling. Diffusion happens because particles move and mix.

Example

In which state do particles move most freely?

Think of steam.

Answer: gas

Example

Why can you smell perfume across a room?

Particles spread out.

Answer: diffusion

Common mistakes

  • Thinking particles get bigger when heated.
  • Thinking there is air between the particles.
  • Thinking particles in a solid do not move at all.

faq.q: Why does a balloon expand in the sun?
faq.a: The gas particles move faster and push harder on the balloon.

faq.q: Why is ice less dense than water?
faq.a: Its particles form an open structure with more space between them.

items.e: Melting, freezing, boiling, condensing and sublimating.

items.q: Which state of matter can easily be squashed (compressed)?

items.q: Bridges have expansion joints with small gaps. Which explains this?
c: The mass of the substance increases when heated.
The bridge can expand on hot days without buckling.
The particles themselves become bigger when heated.
items.e: Particles move faster and further apart when heated; they do not grow and no new particles form.

items.q: A metal lid on a glass jar is held under hot water and then opens easily. Which explains this?
c: The particles themselves become bigger when heated.
The mass of the substance increases when heated.
The metal lid expands more than the glass when heated.
items.e: Particles move faster and further apart when heated; they do not grow and no new particles form.

items.q: A thick glass cup cracks when boiling water is poured into it. Which explains this?
c: The mass of the substance increases when heated.
The particles themselves become bigger when heated.
The inside of the glass expands faster than the outside.
items.e: Particles move faster and further apart when heated; they do not grow and no new particles form.

items.q: How are the particles arranged in a liquid?
c: Closely packed in a fixed, orderly arrangement.
They are all touching in a gas.
Close together but not in fixed positions.
items.e: In a liquid, particles are close together but not in fixed positions and slide past one another.

items.q: Gaps are left between sections of a railway track. Which explains this?
c: The mass of the substance increases when heated.
The steel expands on hot days and needs room to expand.
The particles themselves become bigger when heated.
items.e: Particles move faster and further apart when heated; they do not grow and no new particles form.

items.q: Oxygen moves from the air in the lungs into the blood. What is the best explanation?
c: The water or air particles stopped moving.
Diffusion: oxygen moved from a higher to a lower concentration.
The particles were pushed by convection only.
The particles grew bigger and filled the space.
items.e: Particles are always moving randomly, so there is a net movement from where they are more concentrated to where they are less concentrated.

items.q: A balloon left in the sun gets bigger. Which explains this?
c: The mass of the substance increases when heated.
The air inside expands as its particles move faster and further apart.
The particles themselves become bigger when heated.
items.e: Particles move faster and further apart when heated; they do not grow and no new particles form.

items.q: How are the particles arranged in a solid?
c: Close together but not in fixed positions.
They are all touching in a gas.
Closely packed in a fixed, orderly arrangement.
items.e: In a solid, particles are closely packed in a fixed, orderly arrangement and vibrate about fixed positions.

items.q: You can smell durian from the other end of a room. What is the best explanation?
c: Diffusion: durian smell particles diffused through the air.
The particles grew bigger and filled the space.
The particles were pushed by convection only.
The water or air particles stopped moving.
items.e: Particles are always moving randomly, so there is a net movement from where they are more concentrated to where they are less concentrated.

items.q: Two identical drops of food coloring are added to water at 60 °C and at 80 °C. In which beaker does the color spread faster?
items.e: At a higher temperature, particles move faster, so diffusion is faster.

items.q: How do the particles in a gas move?
c: They do not move at all.
Move quickly and randomly in all directions.
items.e: In a gas, particles are far apart and randomly arranged and move quickly and randomly in all directions.

c: Close together but not in fixed positions.

items.e: In a gas, particles are far apart and randomly arranged and move quickly and randomly in all directions.

items.q: Ammonia gas and hydrogen chloride gas are released at opposite ends of a glass tube. A white ring forms nearer the hydrogen chloride end. What does this show?
c: Ammonia particles diffuse faster because they are lighter.
Both gases diffuse at the same rate.
items.e: Lighter particles move faster at the same temperature.

items.q: A crystal of potassium manganate(VII) is placed in water. A purple color slowly spreads. What is the best explanation?
c: Diffusion: the purple particles moved from a higher to a lower concentration.
The particles were pushed by convection only.
The particles grew bigger and filled the space.
The water or air particles stopped moving.
items.e: Particles are always moving randomly, so there is a net movement from where they are more concentrated to where they are less concentrated.

items.q: The liquid in a thermometer rises when it is warmed. Which explains this?
c: The particles themselves become bigger when heated.
The liquid expands as its particles move further apart.
The mass of the substance increases when heated.
items.e: Particles move faster and further apart when heated; they do not grow and no new particles form.

items.q: In which state does diffusion happen fastest?
c: it is the same in all states
items.e: Gas particles move fastest and are furthest apart.

items.q: Trisha observes sweat drying from your skin. What happens to the motion of the particles?
items.e: Adding energy speeds particles up; removing energy slows them down.

items.q: More air is pumped into a car tire (volume and temperature stay the same). Why does the pressure increase?
c: The particles hit each other more often, not the walls.
The mass of each particle changes.
More particles hit the walls each second.
items.e: Gas pressure comes from particles colliding with the walls of the container.

items.q: More air is pumped into a car tire (volume and temperature stay the same). What happens to the pressure of the gas?
items.e: More particles hit the walls each second.

items.q: A sealed syringe of air is put in a refrigerator. What happens to the pressure of the gas?
items.e: The particles move more slowly, so they hit the walls less often and with less force.

items.q: Which state of matter is described? “The forces of attraction between particles are strongest.”
items.e: Solid: close, regular, vibrate. Liquid: close, random, slide past each other. Gas: far apart, random, fast.

items.q: Which state of matter is described? “Particles move randomly at high speeds in all directions.”
items.e: Solid: close, regular, vibrate. Liquid: close, random, slide past each other. Gas: far apart, random, fast.

items.q: Which state of matter is described? “Particles are far apart in a random arrangement.”
items.e: Solid: close, regular, vibrate. Liquid: close, random, slide past each other. Gas: far apart, random, fast.

items.q: Why is a gas easy to compress?

items.q: What does the temperature of a substance measure?

items.q: Calculate the root-mean-square speed of carbon dioxide molecules (molar mass 0.0440 kg/mol) at 5,800 K.
items.e: ½m crms² = (3/2)kT, crms = √(3kT/m) = 1,810 m/s.

items.q: What happens to the particles of a gas when its temperature rises?
c: They move faster: their average kinetic energy increases.
items.e: The kinetic particle model: all matter is made of tiny particles in constant random motion.

items.q: A bicycle pump's outlet is blocked and the piston is pushed in slowly (constant temperature). What happens to the pressure of the gas?
items.e: The same particles are in a smaller volume, so they hit the walls more often.
